metadata.case_name: NG SHUI ON v. WONG TSUING MING AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: operator of a plastic injection moulding machine

injuries.description: Amputation of left hand and part of left forearm (amputation about 6½inches below the elbow).
injuries.body_part: left hand and part of left forearm
source: the platen suddenly and without warning closed on and crushed his left hand. The injury eventually resulted in the amputation of the Plaintiff's hand and part of his forearm.
an amputation about 6½inches below the elbow.

he said that there were four operations altogether. First the thumb and one finger were amputated. Next another finger plus part of another one were removed. In the third operation, part of the hand went. Finally there was a decision to amputate at the wrist but that was not considered enough so the final amputation was done.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation at level between left elbow and wrist

manifestations.description: The Plaintiff suffers some phantom limb symptoms which acts as an irritant rather than a serious side effect.
Unable to play ballgames such as bowling, table tennis and basketball which he played before the accident.

"an amputation of the arm with a functional below the elbow is a 90% impairment of the arm and a 54% impairment of the whole man "where the preferred arm is affected. In the case of an unpreferred arm, the impairment of the whole man is 50%. I have adopted the figure of 54%.

treatments_received: Four operations culminating in amputation on 1981-02-10
Fitted with two prostheses (an artificial arm and a hook device)
Hospitalised for a total of three and a half months

losses.description: Amputation of the left hand and part of the forearm resulting in substantial permanent impairment (judge adopted figure of 54% impairment of the whole man).

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Before the accident, the Plaintiff played ballgames, such as bowling, table tennis and basketball but can do so no longer.
Difficulty in finding and staying in work after the injury; reduced earnings and subsequent employment as a Toilet Cleaner at lower pay.

comparable_cases.case_name: WONG Pui-kwan v. Artking Industries Ltd.
comparable_cases.injury_description: Crushed right hand (preferred hand). After three operations he had very little left of his hand, losing the thumb and all fingers save for "substantial remnants" of thumb and fifth finger.

Severe crushing injuries of the right hand and forearm left the right hand with only two bones, the fourth and fifth metacarpals, with only the ring and fifth finger remaining, condition almost equivalent to an amputation at mid-hand, a 54% impairment of the whole man.
Amputation of the right preferred hand and part of the forearm to within four inches of the elbow.
